premises.text: Market messaging is stuck in either-text-or-voice tradeoffs
premises.evidence_span: every one of these messages is either in text format or voice format

premises.text: Talks always includes both text and voice, with audio fallback for bad transcriptions
premises.evidence_span: even if the transcription is not perfect, you always have the original audio

premises.text: App expands to rich media and easy Twitter/Facebook sharing
premises.evidence_span: What started off as a simple concept of putting text and voice into every message evolved into a fully featured messaging app

premises.text: Four-platform rollout and no-app-required receiving drive virality
premises.evidence_span: Another major difference between talks and other apps is that talks doesn't require the receiver to have the app

premises.text: Voice cloning personalizes spoken playback of messages and posts
premises.evidence_span: it learns your voice when you speak to the app, and it creates a voice clone of you on the cloud

premises.text: Application is free (with promotional celebrity voices)

value.text: A better way to communicate that always has text and voice together
value.evidence_span: Which is better way to communicate, text or voice?

causal_links.evidence_span: This will help talks be more viral than any other messaging app

notes: Voice cloning kept inside product domain as message-playback feature. Free price with platform virality as commercial/distribution domain.
